product: MCPShield — a managed MCP firewall service sold to AI development agencies and AI-native SaaS companies. Embeds as a middleware layer between their Claude-powered agent workflows and any downstream MCP tool server. Provides per-agent-profile tool scoping, three-way policy decisions (execute / human-approval queue / hard-block), AES-256-GCM credential injection, and a full audit log — all surfaced via a hosted dashboard the agency can white-label or point their enterprise clients at for compliance sign-off.

extract_list.refactor: Replace hard-coded 'shepgate' server name and AGENT_PROFILE_ID env-var pattern with a runtime config object injected at startup so MCPShield can serve multiple tenant agent profiles in a single process. Remove the direct dynamic import of ToolExecutor inside the CallTool handler — wire it at module load time so the dependency is explicit and testable. Rename the file to src/core/mcp-host.ts.

Extract the four-branch decision tree into a pure function (no Prisma calls inside) that accepts a pre-fetched ToolRecord and PermissionRecord. Keep all DB writes in the outer PolicyEngine class so the core logic is unit-testable without a live database. Add an organizationId field to ExecutionRequest to scope audit logs per tenant. Rename to src/core/policy.ts.

Delete all three mock*Execution private methods (mockGitHubExecution, mockFilesystemExecution, mockDatabaseExecution) — they are dev scaffolding and create false confidence. Keep the real-vs-mock flag as USE_MOCK_EXECUTION for CI only, guarded by a NODE_ENV !== 'production' assertion that panics at boot if the flag is set in prod. Rename to src/core/execution.ts.

Replace the hard-coded commonSecretNames list with a per-Server secretNames column read from the DB, so MCPShield can inject only the secrets each downstream server actually declares. Add a per-tenant connection pool keyed on (organizationId, serverId) to prevent cross-tenant connection reuse. Rename to src/core/mcp-client.ts.

Drop the User table (MCPShield uses Clerk for auth, not session passwords). Add an Organization table and foreign key organizationId to AgentProfile, Server, Secret, and ActionLog so all data is tenant-scoped from day one. Add a secretNames TEXT[] column to Server for per-server secret injection scoping. Add indexes on ActionLog(organizationId, createdAt) and PendingAction(organizationId, status) for the dashboard query patterns.

icp: CTOs and lead engineers at AI development agencies (10–50 engineers) and AI-native SaaS companies embedding Claude agent workflows into enterprise client deliverables, who are losing or stalling deals because the enterprise buyer demands a demonstrated governance, approval, and audit layer before signing.
wedge: Ship governed AI agents to enterprise clients in days — hand them a live audit log and one-tap approval workflow on day one instead of spending six weeks building compliance scaffolding from scratch.
rough_dev_effort: 8–10 focused days for a single senior engineer. The core proxy + policy engine + secrets store is already real and functional — roughly 60% of the backend logic is lifted. The remaining work is: tenant isolation (2 days), REST API surface (2 days), dashboard UI (2 days), auth wiring + MCP host process runner (1 day), polish and tests (2 days). First demo-able build (proxy + approval queue + audit log, no white-label) reachable in 4–5 days.
